name: vt-v1
prompt:
In requirements.txt replace the two lines `webrtcvad                        # Voice Activity Detection (requires compiler)` and `cffi                             # Required by webrtcvad` with exactly these three lines:
webrtcvad; sys_platform != "win32"   # Voice Activity Detection (needs a C compiler)
webrtcvad-wheels; sys_platform == "win32"   # same module name, prebuilt Windows wheels
cffi                             # Required by webrtcvad
No text before a `;` other than the package name. Change nothing else. One SEARCH/REPLACE block.

name: vt-v2a
prompt:
In setup.bat replace these lines:
REM Check Python
echo Checking Python installation...
python --version >nul 2>&1
with:
REM Check Python (prefer 3.12: torch, onnxruntime etc. have no wheels for newer versions)
echo Checking Python installation...
set "PY=python"
py -3.12 --version >nul 2>&1
if not errorlevel 1 set "PY=py -3.12"
%PY% --version >nul 2>&1
Change nothing else. One SEARCH/REPLACE block.

name: vt-v2b
prompt: In setup.bat the line `for /f "tokens=2" %%i in ('python --version 2^>^&1') do set PYTHON_VERSION=%%i` must call `%PY%` instead of `python`: replace `'python --version 2^>^&1'` with `'%PY% --version 2^>^&1'`. Change nothing else. One SEARCH/REPLACE block; SEARCH only that for line.

name: vt-v2c
prompt: In setup.bat replace the line `    python -m venv venv` with `    %PY% -m venv venv`. Change nothing else. One SEARCH/REPLACE block.

name: vt-v2d
prompt:
In setup.bat replace the block that starts with `REM Warn about Python 3.14` and ends with its closing `)` (the one printing `[WARNING] Python 3.14 detected.`) by:
REM Warn about Python 3.13 and newer
echo %PYTHON_VERSION% | findstr /R /C:"^3\.1[3-9]" >nul
if not errorlevel 1 (
    echo.
    echo [WARNING] Python %PYTHON_VERSION% detected. torch, onnxruntime and others have no wheels yet.
    echo           Install Python 3.12 ^(py -3.12 is used automatically when present^).
)
Change nothing else. One SEARCH/REPLACE block.

name: vt-v3
prompt: In setup.bat rewrite the pip section from `echo Installing core dependencies...` up to the line `echo [OK] Dependencies installed` plus the blank `echo.` after it. New logic: `set "PIP_FAILED=0"`; `pip install -r requirements.txt`; on `if errorlevel 1 (` print the existing [WARNING] and then install one by one: vosk, sounddevice, "numpy<2.0", requests, translators, "gradio>=4.44.0", argostranslate, websockets, moonshine-voice, tokenizers, huggingface_hub, and `pip install webrtcvad-wheels` (each line `pip install X` followed by `if errorlevel 1 set "PIP_FAILED=1"`). After that block: `if "%PIP_FAILED%"=="1" (` print `[ERROR] Dependencies could not be installed. See the pip output above.`, `pause`, `exit /b 1` `)`; then `echo [OK] Dependencies installed` and `echo.`. The [OK] line must be reached only when nothing failed. Note: when requirements.txt itself installs fine, PIP_FAILED stays 0. One SEARCH/REPLACE block.

name: vt-v4
prompt: In setup.bat rewrite the `REM Check for models` block (from `REM Check for models` up to, not including, the line `echo ========================================` before `echo Setup complete!`). Facts: models live in the `vosk_models` folder (not `models`), the downloader is `download_vosk_models.py` (use `python download_vosk_models.py --lang en-us --small`). Rules for cmd: every `(` and `)` inside an echo line must be written `^(` and `^)`; do not use `set /p` or `%choice%` — use `choice /c yn /m "Download a small English model ^(40 MB^)?"` and then `if errorlevel 2 (` ... `) else (` ... `)` where errorlevel 2 means No. Also create the vosk_models folder check: `dir /b vosk_models 2>nul | findstr /r "." >nul`. Messages: no models -> [WARNING], ask; yes -> download command; no -> tell the user the manual command `python download_vosk_models.py --lang en-us --small` and the URL https://alphacephei.com/vosk/models; models found -> `[OK] Models found:` and `dir /b vosk_models`. One SEARCH/REPLACE block.

name: vt-v6
prompt: In start.bat replace the line `python voice_translator.py` with `python voice_translator.py --host 127.0.0.1` so Windows does not show a firewall prompt (the app's default 0.0.0.0 stays for Docker). Change nothing else. One SEARCH/REPLACE block.
